title: Kitchen and Tide
premise: Emrys Dravenmoor inherited her family's failing vineyard along with its crushing debts, and the annual Harvest Festival is her last chance to save it. When a snowstorm traps her with two rivals from her past — Julian Ashe, the investor who broke her heart, and Marguerite Voss, the sommelier-turned-competitor bidding to buy the vineyard out from under her — old betrayals resurface alongside undeniable chemistry. As sabotage, forged contracts, and a hidden will threaten everything, Emrys discovers the corruption runs through someone she trusted most. In the end she chooses truth over loyalty, exposes the betrayal at the festival's final tasting, keeps the vineyard on her own terms, and risks her whole heart with Julian — not because the timing improved, but because she finally did.
about_author: Kestrel Halloran spent a decade working restaurant kitchens in coastal wine country before turning to fiction full-time. She writes stories about stubborn women, second chances, and the places that shape us whether we like it or not.

chapters.title: Debts Instead of Grapes
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Emrys surveys the frost-bitten vineyard and the stack of foreclosure notices, establishing her cynicism about second chances. Her grandmother's festival invitation arrives with an ominous note: 'Someone is coming.' Emotional beat: weary defiance masking fear of losing the only home she has left.

chapters.title: The Guest List
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Preparations for the Harvest Festival begin; Emrys learns the bank sent a representative and that Marguerite Voss, now a celebrated sommelier, requested a private tour. A cryptic phone call hints at a rival bid already in motion. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into competitive resolve.

chapters.title: Snowfall and Old Wounds
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Julian Ashe arrives early to inspect the property for his firm, recognizing the vineyard — and expecting Emrys. Flashbacks reveal their history: the best mistake of their twenties, ended by his silence when her family needed him. Emotional beat: guilt he's never confessed, disguised as businesslike detachment.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The storm hits early; roads close, trapping Emrys, Julian, and Marguerite at the estate with no cell service. The three are forced to share dinner in the crumbling great hall. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension crackling with unfinished history.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Knows
chapters.summary: Marguerite POV. Marguerite privately reveals to Emrys that she isn't just a buyer — she's investigating the bank officer who pushed the Dravenmoor loans into default. She asks for Emrys's trust; Emrys gives her caution instead. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming over shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Cellar Confessions
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Trapped by the storm, Emrys and Julian get drunk on the oldest bottle in the cellar and finally argue about what happened ten years ago. He admits he was ordered to walk away; she admits she never stopped wondering. Emotional beat: anger burning down into something dangerously tender.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Marguerite POV. Marguerite finds loan documents bearing Emrys's signature dated while she was abroad — evidence of fraud. Before she can show Emrys, someone ransacks her room. Emotional beat: the investigation turns personal and dangerous.

chapters.title: Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The snow melts enough for one car to leave; Julian chooses to stay, claiming the deal requires it. Emrys catches herself hoping, then hardens. Her foreman, Dane, urges her to sell and be done with it. Emotional beat: hope rekindling against her own better judgment.

chapters.title: Dane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Reconciling accounts, Emrys finds payments funneled to an account she doesn't recognize — signed off by Dane. When questioned, he deflects smoothly. Emotional beat: first crack in her trust of the person closest to her.

chapters.title: Tasting Notes
chapters.summary: Marguerite POV. Marguerite hosts a comparative tasting of the vineyard's reserve wines versus her own label, publicly praising the Dravenmoor terroir — a strategic move that spites the bank and stuns Emrys. Julian watches Emrys shine. Emotional beat: unexpected generosity complicating the rivalry.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The bank officer, Mr. Corliss, arrives uninvited with a buyout offer timed to kill the festival. Julian openly opposes his own firm's terms, burning professional bridges. Emotional beat: Julian choosing Emrys over his career, and both of them knowing it.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Dane POV. Dane confronts Corliss in secret — revealing he's been feeding information under duress, his sister's medical debts held over him. He destroys evidence to protect himself. Emotional beat: a good man justifying a small betrayal that will cost everything.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The grounds fill with vendors and neighbors; the festival opens beautifully despite everything. Emrys and Julian share a near-kiss interrupted by news: Marguerite has been seen meeting Corliss. Emotional beat: joy undercut by the return of doubt.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Anonymous photos show Marguerite and Corliss together; Emrys confronts her, and Marguerite refuses to explain, protecting her source. Their alliance shatters. Emotional beat: betrayal felt most sharply because hope had been allowed in.

chapters.title: Fire in the East Field
chapters.summary: Julian POV. A fire damages the festival pavilion overnight; Julian pulls Emrys from the smoke. Evidence points inside the house. Julian realizes the fraud, the leak, and the arson connect — and suspects someone Emrys loves. Emotional beat: protective urgency, terror of telling her the truth.

chapters.title: Whole Heart or Pieces
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Julian tells Emrys everything he's found, including his own role in the original loan scheme years ago. She must decide whether love offered late is worth anything. She chooses to hear him fully — lending no pieces this time. Emotional beat: the book's thematic heart; vulnerability as strength.

chapters.title: The Hidden Will
chapters.summary: Marguerite POV. Marguerite decodes her real reason for coming: her mentor was Emrys's grandmother's lost friend, and the grandmother's true will left Emrys the vineyard free of debt — suppressed by Corliss and an accomplice inside the house. Emotional beat: revelation reframing every prior betrayal.

chapters.title: Accomplice
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The suppressed will's witness signature belongs to Dane. Confronted with Marguerite's evidence and his own burned ledger, Dane confesses — coerced by Corliss, complicit in the forgery. Emotional beat: grief for a friendship corrupted by desperation and power.

chapters.title: The Final Tasting
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. At the festival's closing ceremony, before the crowd and the bank's lawyers, Emrys presents the true will, the forged documents, and Dane's testimony. Corliss is exposed; the debt collapses. Emotional beat: triumph earned not by power but by choosing truth over comfortable lies.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Julian POV. Corliss faces investigation; Dane takes responsibility and leaves to make amends. Julian formally withdraws his firm's claim and offers himself — plainly, without leverage or timing excuses. Emotional beat: humility as the price of a second chance.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Press
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Weeks later, the ice-wine harvest begins under new ownership: Emrys's, with Marguerite as partner. Emrys and Julian plant a new vine together on the east field where the fire burned. Emotional beat: quiet joy; belonging chosen rather than inherited.

chapters.title: Kitchen and Tide
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. One year later at the next festival, Emrys cooks in the estate kitchen with Julian, Marguerite, and a forgiven-but-changed Dane at the table. She reflects that tides return and kitchens refill — and that she risked the whole heart, and it held. Emotional beat: full-circle resolution, warm and earned.
